This article reproduces, with every call visible, the regional-consistency strategy of the
mrct-consistency technical report: a multiregional trial is positive overall, one region looks
unfavourable, and a subgroup identified by `forestsearch()` **on the patients outside the region** is
applied inside it. It is condensed from the report's chapters on the setting, the case example, the
analytic layer and the simulation campaign. Every number below is computed here, by forestsearch, or
read from a small record shipped with the article (`vignettes/articles/mrct-consistency/`, with the
commit and source path of each file in its `PROVENANCE.md`); the report's derivations are cited, not
repeated.

# Overview: the question and the design {#sec-overview}

## The trigger and the question

A global trial meets its primary endpoint: the upper 95% limit of the all-patient Cox hazard ratio is
below 1.0 (**ITT ub < 1.0**). One region, about a fifth of the patients, has a Cox point estimate
above 1.0 (**region ITT > 1.0**). The pair, in the same trial, is the **trigger**: the regional
consistency failure as it presents in oncology multiregional trials. Region ITT > 1.0 describes a point
estimate; no regulator codifies it as a threshold for harm.

Two explanations fit a trigger: the region differs in its treatment effect, or the trial contains a
subgroup that is harmed, present in every region, and the region's estimate is pulled up by it (with
the region's prognosis and the finite follow-up window shaping how far). The question is whether a
subgroup identified on the non-region patients can explain the regional result: if removing it from the
region leaves a Cox estimate below 1.0, the regional result is compatible with a trial-wide subgroup
and is not evidence of a region-specific effect. The strategy is **signal generation, not
confirmation**.

## The pipeline, for one trial

1. Fit the all-patient Cox model of treatment. If ITT ub $\ge$ 1.0, stop: the trial is not positive.
2. Fit the region's Cox model. If region ITT $\le$ 1.0, stop: the trigger is not reached.
3. Run the identifier, `forestsearch()`, on the non-region patients. It declares a subgroup $\hat H$,
   a rule in at most two baseline covariates, or nothing.
4. Apply $\hat H$ inside the region; $\hat G$ = region minus $\hat H$. Fit the region's Cox model on
   $\hat G$.
5. Record whether region($\hat G$) < 1.0; the trigger together with region($\hat G$) < 1.0 is
   **joint**. Record, as the oracle, whether region($G^*$) < 1.0, with $G^*$ = region minus the true
   harmed subgroup $H^*$. In simulation, also record the sensitivity and specificity of $\hat H$
   against $H^*$ on both sides.

$\hat H$ is learned on the non-region patients only and applied to the region, whose outcomes the
identifier never sees: the region is a held-out test set, and its Cox fits on the whole region and on
$\hat G$ are ordinary Wald fits on sets defined by a fixed rule. The non-region estimate inside
$\hat H$ is selected; @sec-rep5-mr bounds it by multiplier resampling.

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| trigger | ITT ub < 1.0 and region ITT > 1.0, in the same trial |
| $H^*$ | the true harmed subgroup, here CD4 $\le$ 230 cells/mm³ |
| $\hat H$ | the subgroup the identifier declares on the non-region patients |
| $\hat G$, $G^*$ | region minus $\hat H$; region minus $H^*$ (the oracle) |
| $\hat H^c$ | the non-region complement of $\hat H$: non-region patients not in $\hat H$ (not $\hat G$) |
| joint | the trigger and region($\hat G$) < 1.0; with $G^*$ in place of $\hat G$, the oracle joint |
| Sens / Spec | of $\hat H$ against $H^*$, on the non-region patients and in the region |
| AHR | average hazard ratio of a set: $\exp$ of its patients' mean log hazard ratio |
| CDE | controlled direct effect: the ratio of the set's mean hazards under the two arms |
| margHR(40), margHR($\infty$) | the marginal hazard ratio: the limit of the set's two-sample Cox estimate at the 40-month analysis, and with no censoring |

: Labels used throughout.

## The data-generating mechanism, built from ACTG 175 {#sec-dgm}

A Weibull accelerated-failure-time model is fitted to a published trial and expanded to a
super-population of 20,000 rows by a Gaussian copula. A region of about 20% of patients is planted by
a logistic model with odds ratio 3 on symptomatic status and no CD4 term, and its baseline hazard is
shifted by $r$; every patient's hazard ratio is $b = 0.55$ outside $H^*$ = {CD4 $\le$ 230} and $h$
inside it, in every region; all hazards are then multiplied by $m = 3$. Three calls build it, shown
here as a reader would make them with their own trial.

**1. The trial data.** ACTG 175 (`speff2trial`), arms ZDV + ddI (`arms == 1`, experimental) and ddI
alone (`arms == 3`, control). The outcome is `days` to the composite endpoint, in months, with event
indicator `cens`; the prognostic covariates are age, weight (`wtkg`), Karnofsky score (`karnof`),
days of prior antiretroviral therapy (`preanti`), baseline CD4 (`cd40`) and CD8 (`cd80`) counts, and
the binary haemophilia (`hemo`), homosexual activity (`homo`), drug use (`drugs`), race, gender and
symptomatic status (`symptom`).

```{r reader-data}
#| code-fold: show
actg <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))
actg$treat_mrct <- as.integer(actg$arms == 1L)   # ZDV + ddI = 1, ddI = 0
actg$time_months <- actg$days / 30.4375
rownames(actg) <- NULL
c(patients = nrow(actg), events = sum(actg$cens), experimental = sum(actg$treat_mrct))
```

**2. The region and the harmed subgroup.** `inject_mrct_structure()` fits the Weibull model on the
twelve covariates, expands it by the copula, plants the region (`region`: prevalence, the logistic
model's odds ratios, the prognostic log hazard ratio $r$) and the harmed subgroup (`spline_spec` sets
$b$ everywhere; `x3` multiplies it by $h/b$ in CD4 $\le$ 230), here for cell S2 ($h = 2$). The
copula's latent correlation is fitted live by latentcor (Suggests); without latentcor the call warns
and uses the normal-score correlation instead, which gives a valid but different super-population.

```{r reader-dgm}
#| code-fold: show
#| warning: true
dgm_live <- inject_mrct_structure(
  actg,
  outcome_var = "time_months", event_var = "cens", treatment_var = "treat_mrct",
  continuous_vars = c("age", "wtkg", "karnof", "preanti", "cd40", "cd80"),
  factor_vars = c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom"),
  x_pred = "cd40",
  spline_spec = list(knot = 300, zeta = 800, log_hrs = rep(log(0.55), 3)),  # b = 0.55
  region = list(prevalence = 0.20, or_pred = 1, x1_vars = "symptom", or_x1 = 3,
                loghr = -log(4),                                          # r
                band = list(cut = 230, or = 1)),
  x3 = list(vars = "cd40", cuts = list(cd40 = 230), loghr = log(2 / 0.55)),  # h = 2 in H*
  region_treat_loghr = NULL,
  n_super = 20000, expand = "copula", seed = 7L,
  continuous_vars_cens = c("age", "cd40"), factor_vars_cens = "symptom")
```

**3. The hazard scale.** `scale_dgm_hazard()` multiplies every hazard by $m$ and leaves every hazard
ratio unchanged.

```{r reader-scale}
#| code-fold: show
dgm_live <- scale_dgm_hazard(dgm_live, m = 3)
c(rows = nrow(dgm_live$df_super), region = mean(dgm_live$df_super$z_region),
  Hstar = mean(dgm_live$df_super$flag_harm))
```

**To use your own trial**, change these and nothing else:

- the data frame and its outcome, event and treatment names (`outcome_var`, `event_var`,
  `treatment_var`; treatment coded 1 = experimental);
- the covariates (`continuous_vars`, `factor_vars`, binary factors coded 0/1, and the censoring
  model's `continuous_vars_cens`, `factor_vars_cens`);
- the region model (`region`: its prevalence, the covariates that predict membership and their odds
  ratios, its prognostic log hazard ratio $r$);
- $H^*$ and its effects: the covariate and cut that define it (`x3`, `region$band`), $b$ outside it
  (`spline_spec$log_hrs`) and $h$ inside it (`x3$loghr` $= \log(h/b)$);
- the analysis window and entry: the analysis time and the uniform entry period used below
  (`analysis_time = 40`, `max_entry = 11`), and `cens_adjust` for the dropout model.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Reproducing this report's build exactly

This chunk exists only so that the committed record is reproduced to the last digit on any platform:
it builds the cells with the latent correlation stored with the campaign's build (`latent_R.csv`,
passed as `latent_R`), so no latentcor fit is made. A reader never needs it. Everything from the
build check onward uses the cells built here (`build_cell()`).

```{r build-fn}
#| code-fold: show
latent_R <- as.matrix(rd("latent_R.csv", row.names = 1))

# One cell: hazard ratio h in H* = {CD4 <= 230}, b = 0.55 elsewhere, region
# prognostic log-HR r, all hazards x m; the calls of steps 2 and 3 above.
build_cell <- function(h, r = -log(4), b = 0.55, cut = 230, m = 3) {
  w <- character(0)
  dgm <- withCallingHandlers(
    inject_mrct_structure(
      actg,
      outcome_var = "time_months", event_var = "cens", treatment_var = "treat_mrct",
      continuous_vars = c("age", "wtkg", "karnof", "preanti", "cd40", "cd80"),
      factor_vars = c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom"),
      x_pred = "cd40",
      spline_spec = list(knot = 300, zeta = 800, log_hrs = rep(log(b), 3)),
      region = list(prevalence = 0.20, or_pred = 1, x1_vars = "symptom", or_x1 = 3,
                    loghr = r, band = list(cut = cut, or = 1)),
      x3 = list(vars = "cd40", cuts = list(cd40 = cut), loghr = log(h / b)),
      region_treat_loghr = NULL,
      n_super = 20000, expand = "copula", seed = 7L,
      continuous_vars_cens = c("age", "cd40"), factor_vars_cens = "symptom",
      latent_R = latent_R),
    warning = function(cnd) { w <<- c(w, conditionMessage(cnd)); invokeRestart("muffleWarning") })
  dgm <- scale_dgm_hazard(dgm, m = m)
  attr(dgm, "build_warnings") <- w
  dgm
}
t_build <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
dgm_S2 <- build_cell(h = 2)
t_build <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_build
# the live fit of step 2 against the shipped matrix
R_live <- dgm_live$mrct$latent_R
R_diff <- if (is.null(R_live)) NA_real_ else max(abs(R_live[rownames(latent_R), colnames(latent_R)] - latent_R))
live_same <- isTRUE(R_diff == 0) && identical(dgm_live$df_super, dgm_S2$df_super)
c(seconds = round(t_build, 1), rows = nrow(dgm_S2$df_super), latent_R_max_abs_diff = R_diff,
  super_population_identical = live_same)
```

`r if (live_same) "On this render machine the live fit of step 2 equals the shipped matrix exactly (largest absolute difference 0) and the two super-populations are identical, so the reader's path and this chunk give the same build." else sprintf("On this render machine the live fit of step 2 differs from the shipped matrix (largest absolute difference %s), so the reader's path gives a slightly different super-population; the checks below use this chunk's build.", format(R_diff, digits = 2))`
:::

**Build check.** The build must equal the campaign's build record of S2
(`build_full_summary.csv`, the `S2_rmlog4` row) in every numeric column that describes the build;
the article stops otherwise.

```{r build-check}
pop_S2 <- ahr_population(dgm_S2, analysis_time = 40, max_entry = 11)
e_reg <- ahr_limit(pop_S2, "region", b = 0.55, h = 2, variance = FALSE)
e_non <- ahr_limit(pop_S2, "nonregion", b = 0.55, h = 2, variance = FALSE)
ds <- dgm_S2$df_super; reg_s <- ds$z_region == 1; Hs_s <- ds$flag_harm == 1; rg <- dgm_S2$mrct$region
ours <- c(
  h = 2, r = -log(4), mu = unname(dgm_S2$model_params$mu), mu_fitted = unname(dgm_S2$mrct$mu_fitted),
  tau = dgm_S2$model_params$tau, m = dgm_S2$mrct$hazard_multiplier,
  b0_z_region = unname(dgm_S2$model_params$b0["z_region"]), b0_treat = unname(dgm_S2$model_params$b0["treat"]),
  b0_treat_harm = unname(dgm_S2$model_params$b0["treat_harm"]),
  prognostic_loghr_recorded = rg$prognostic_loghr, region_alpha0 = rg$alpha0,
  region_coef_cd40 = unname(rg$coefs["cd40"]), region_coef_symptom = unname(rg$coefs["symptom"]),
  region_coef_cd4_le_230 = log(rg$band$or), prevalence = mean(reg_s),
  Hstar_share_region = mean(Hs_s[reg_s]), Hstar_share_nonregion = mean(Hs_s[!reg_s]),
  event_prob_40_region = e_reg$d, event_prob_40_nonregion = e_non$d,
  events_n1000_region = 1000 * mean(reg_s) * e_reg$d, events_n1000_nonregion = 1000 * mean(!reg_s) * e_non$d,
  mean_theta0_region = mean(ds$theta_0[reg_s]), mean_theta0_nonregion = mean(ds$theta_0[!reg_s]),
  n_build_warnings = length(attr(dgm_S2, "build_warnings")))
br <- rd("build_full_summary.csv"); br <- br[br$cell == "S2_rmlog4", ]
num_cols <- names(br)[vapply(br, is.numeric, NA)]
stopifnot(nrow(br) == 1,
          setequal(setdiff(num_cols, names(ours)), c("prevalence_trials", "seed", "truth_seed", "replicates")),
          isTRUE(all.equal(unname(ours), unname(unlist(br[names(ours)])), tolerance = 1e-8)),
          all((ds$z_cd40 <= 230) == (ds$flag_harm == 1)))
build_diff <- max(abs(ours - unlist(br[names(ours)])) / pmax(1, abs(unlist(br[names(ours)]))))
c(columns_compared = length(ours), largest_relative_difference = signif(build_diff, 2))
```

**Passed**: the build equals the record (largest relative difference `r format(build_diff, digits = 2)`).
In this build the region holds `r pc(mean(reg_s))`% of the super-population, $H^*$ holds
`r pc(mean(Hs_s))`% of all patients (`r pc(mean(Hs_s[reg_s]))`% of the region and
`r pc(mean(Hs_s[!reg_s]))`% outside it), and at equal covariates a region patient has
$e^{r}$ = `r f2(exp(unname(dgm_S2$model_params$b0["z_region"])))` times the hazard of a non-region
patient. The trial: $n = 1{,}000$, 1:1, entry uniform over 11 months, analysis at 40 months; the
Weibull dropout is pushed far beyond the window (`cens_adjust = 50`), so all censoring is
administrative.

## The cells

Six cells at $r = -\log 4$ differ only in the hazard ratio $h$ inside $H^*$; two later-enrolling cells
keep S2's effects and let the region enter later, with $r$ or the delay solved so that
P(trigger) = 0.25 (@sec-roots). The specifications as the committed runs' timing records state them:

```{r cells}
tf <- rd("timing_full.csv"); ts1 <- rd("timing_S1.csv"); te <- rd("timing_entry_cells.csv")
cells <- rbind(
  data.frame(cell = sub("_rmlog4$", "", tf$setting), h = tf$h, r = -log(4), delay = 0, n = 1000,
             replicates = tf$replicates, seed = tf$seed),
  data.frame(cell = "S1", h = ts1$h[ts1$setting == "S1_rmlog4"], r = -log(4), delay = 0, n = 1000,
             replicates = ts1$replicates[ts1$setting == "S1_rmlog4"], seed = ts1$seed[ts1$setting == "S1_rmlog4"]),
  data.frame(cell = te$setting, h = te$h, r = te$r, delay = te$a, n = te$n, replicates = te$replicates,
             seed = te$seed))
cells <- cells[match(c("N0", "N1", "S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S2_D1", "S2_D2"), cells$cell), ]
rownames(cells) <- NULL
# the shipped build record's h and r for the five full cells
bfull <- rd("build_full_summary.csv")
stopifnot(!anyNA(cells$cell), near(bfull$h, cells$h[match(sub("_rmlog4$", "", bfull$cell), cells$cell)]),
          near(bfull$r, -log(4), 1e-12))
find <- ifelse(cells$h == 0.55, "nothing: the same benefit everywhere",
               ifelse(cells$h < 1, "nothing harmful: less benefit in CD4 ≤ 230",
                      ifelse(cells$h == 1, "nothing harmful: no effect in CD4 ≤ 230", "harm in CD4 ≤ 230")))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  cell = cells$cell, `HR in CD4 ≤ 230; elsewhere` = sprintf("%s; 0.55", formatC(cells$h, format = "fg")),
  `what there is to find` = find,
  `region prognostic shift` = sprintf("r = −log %s", formatC(exp(-cells$r), format = "fg", digits = 4)),
  `region enrols later by` = ifelse(cells$delay == 0, "—", sprintf("%s months", f2(cells$delay))),
  n = big(cells$n), replicates = big(cells$replicates), `call seed` = cells$seed, check.names = FALSE),
  align = "lllllrrr", caption = "The cells. Every patient's hazard ratio is the same in every region.")
```

## The analytic layer in brief {#sec-analytic}

For any patient set of such a DGM, analysed at a calendar time with uniform staggered entry and
administrative censoring only, the analytic layer computes by quadrature (nothing is drawn) the exact
limit of the two-sample Cox estimate on the set (the Struthers–Kalbfleisch root, margHR(40)), its
information and robust variance, the expected events, the correlation between nested sets'
estimates, the set's AHR and CDE, and the normal-approximation probability of the trigger at a trial
size. `ahr_population()` reads the DGM; `ahr_limit()` gives a set's four truths; `ahr_design()` gives
the trial-level probabilities; `ahr_solve()` solves P(trigger) = target in one free parameter.
@sec-appendix states the formulas.

```{r analytic-cells}
t_an <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
cells6 <- cells[cells$delay == 0, ]
dgms <- lapply(setNames(cells6$h, cells6$cell), function(h) if (h == 2) dgm_S2 else build_cell(h = h))
pops <- lapply(dgms, ahr_population, analysis_time = 40, max_entry = 11)
sets4 <- c(all = "all patients", nonregion = "non-region", region = "region", region_Gstar = "G* (region minus H*)")
truths <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pops), function(k) {
  h <- cells6$h[cells6$cell == k]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(sets4), function(s) {
    e <- ahr_limit(pops[[k]], s, b = 0.55, h = h, variance = FALSE)
    data.frame(cell = k, set = s, marghr_40 = e$hr, marghr_inf = e$marghr_inf, ahr = e$ahr, cde = e$cde)
  }))
}))
# against the committed predictions (the analytic records of the campaign)
pred <- rbind(rd("predictions_full.csv"), rd("predictions_S1.csv"))
pv <- function(cell, q, set) { v <- pred$value[pred$cell == cell & pred$quantity == q & pred$set == set]; stopifnot(length(v) == 1); v }
tr_ref <- mapply(function(c, s, q) pv(paste0(c, "_rmlog4"), q, s),
                 rep(truths$cell, 4), rep(truths$set, 4),
                 rep(c("marghr_40", "marghr_inf", "ahr", "cde"), each = nrow(truths)))
stopifnot(near(unlist(truths[c("marghr_40", "marghr_inf", "ahr", "cde")]), tr_ref))
tt <- truths
tt$set <- sets4[tt$set]; tt[3:6] <- lapply(tt[3:6], f3)
reg_S2 <- truths[truths$cell == "S2" & truths$set == "region", ]
stopifnot(reg_S2$marghr_40 < 1, reg_S2$cde > 1)
knitr::kable(setNames(tt, c("cell", "set", "margHR(40)", "margHR(∞)", "AHR", "CDE")), row.names = FALSE,
             align = "llrrrr", caption = "The four truths of four sets in the six cells at r = −log 4 (ahr_limit()); equal to the committed predictions to 1e-9.")
```

The four truths differ, and the difference is the point. The AHR and the CDE depend on a set only
through its $H^*$ shares; the two marginal ratios are bounded in $h$ and depend on the window and the
prognostic structure. In S2 the region's margHR(40) is
`r f3(truths$marghr_40[truths$cell == "S2" & truths$set == "region"])`, below 1, although its CDE is
`r f3(truths$cde[truths$cell == "S2" & truths$set == "region"])`: the trigger in S2 is a sampling event
around a regional limit below 1.

**The trigger predictions at $n = 1{,}000$**, and the oracle joint, P(trigger and region($G^*$) < 1.0):

```{r design-n1000}
design_tab <- function(n, cells_k, pops_k, ref_cell) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pops_k), function(k) {
    h <- cells_k$h[cells_k$cell == k]
    p <- ahr_design(pops_k[[k]], b = 0.55, h = h, n = n)$prob
    data.frame(cell = k, n = n, p_A = p[["p_itt_ub_lt1"]], p_B = p[["p_region_itt_gt1"]],
               p_A_B = p[["p_trigger"]], p_Cstar = p[["p_region_Gstar_lt1"]],
               p_A_B_Cstar = p[["p_trigger_and_Gstar_lt1"]], ref = ref_cell(k))
  }))
}
d1000 <- design_tab(1000, cells6, pops, function(k) paste0(k, "_rmlog4"))
for (q in c("p_A", "p_B", "p_A_B", "p_Cstar", "p_A_B_Cstar"))
  stopifnot(all(abs(d1000[[q]] - vapply(d1000$ref, function(cc) pv(cc, q, ""), 0)) < 1e-9))
show_design <- function(d) knitr::kable(data.frame(
  cell = d$cell, `P(ITT ub < 1.0)` = f3(d$p_A), `P(region ITT > 1.0)` = f3(d$p_B), `P(trigger)` = f3(d$p_A_B),
  `P(region(G*) < 1.0)` = f3(d$p_Cstar), `P(oracle joint)` = f3(d$p_A_B_Cstar),
  `P(G* < 1.0 | trigger)` = f3(d$p_A_B_Cstar / d$p_A_B), check.names = FALSE),
  row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrrr")
show_design(d1000)
```

At $n = 700$ (predictions only; the $n = 700$ campaign is in the report and is not reproduced here):

```{r design-n700}
pred700 <- rbind(rd("predictions_n700.csv"), rd("predictions_S1.csv"))
pv7 <- function(cell, q) { v <- pred700$value[pred700$cell == cell & pred700$quantity == q & pred700$set == ""]; stopifnot(length(v) == 1); v }
d700 <- design_tab(700, cells6, pops, function(k) paste0(k, "_rmlog4_n700"))
for (q in c("p_A", "p_B", "p_A_B", "p_Cstar", "p_A_B_Cstar"))
  stopifnot(all(abs(d700[[q]] - vapply(d700$ref, pv7, 0, q = q)) < 1e-9))
show_design(d700)
reg_lt1 <- truths$cell[truths$set == "region" & truths$marghr_40 < 1]
stopifnot(all(d700$p_B[d700$cell %in% reg_lt1] > d1000$p_B[d1000$cell %in% reg_lt1]))
```

Both tables equal the committed predictions to $10^{-9}$. In the cells whose regional limit is below 1
(`r paste(reg_lt1, collapse = ", ")`), P(region ITT > 1.0) is larger at $n = 700$ than at
$n = 1{,}000$: there the trigger is a small-sample event, made frequent by the region's few events.

### How $r = -\log 4$ was chosen, and the later-enrolling regions {#sec-roots}

The campaign's regional shift was chosen to make the trigger frequent at the design: with S2's effects
($h = 2$), $r$ solving P(trigger) = 0.25 at $n = 1{,}000$ is found by `ahr_solve()`, and the campaign
rounded it to $-\log 4$. Each evaluation rebuilds the DGM at that $r$.

```{r root-r}
p_trig_r <- function(r, delay = NULL) {
  d <- build_cell(h = 2, r = r)
  ahr_design(ahr_population(d, 40, 11, entry_delay = delay), b = 0.55, h = 2, n = 1000)$prob[["p_trigger"]]
}
roots <- rd("entry_roots.csv")
rref <- function(tag) { x <- roots[startsWith(roots$row, tag), ]; stopifnot(nrow(x) == 1); x }
sol_r <- ahr_solve(p_trig_r, 0.25, c(-log(5), -log(3.5)), n_scan = 5L, tol = 1e-10)
ref0 <- rref("Reference: a = 0, r solving")
stopifnot(sol_r$n_roots == 1, abs(sol_r$roots - ref0$r) < 1e-6)
c(root_r = sol_r$roots, k_in_minus_log_k = exp(-sol_r$roots), committed_root = ref0$r,
  P_trigger_at_root = sol_r$values)
```

The root is $r = -\log `r formatC(exp(-sol_r$roots), format = "f", digits = 3)`$, the committed
`r f4(ref0$r)`; the campaign used $r = -\log 4$, where P(trigger) is
`r f3(d1000$p_A_B[d1000$cell == "S2"])`. The same target defines the two later-enrolling cells, in
which the region's patients enter $a$ months after the others (`entry_delay`): D1 keeps
$r = -\log 2$ and solves the delay $a$; D2 fixes $a = 6$ months and solves $r$.

```{r root-entry}
dgm_r2 <- build_cell(h = 2, r = -log(2))
p_trig_a <- function(a) ahr_design(ahr_population(dgm_r2, 40, 11, entry_delay = list(var = "z_region", delay = a)),
                                   b = 0.55, h = 2, n = 1000)$prob[["p_trigger"]]
sol_a <- ahr_solve(p_trig_a, 0.25, c(11, 12), scan = c(11, 12), tol = 1e-8)
sol_r6 <- ahr_solve(p_trig_r, 0.25, c(-log(3.5), -log(2.5)), n_scan = 5L, tol = 1e-10,
                    delay = list(var = "z_region", delay = 6))
d1r <- rref("D1:"); d2r <- rref("D2:")
stopifnot(sol_a$n_roots == 1, abs(sol_a$roots - d1r$a) < 1e-6,
          sol_r6$n_roots == 1, abs(sol_r6$roots - d2r$r) < 1e-6)
# the design layer at the two roots, against the committed root records
dD <- lapply(list(S2_D1 = list(r = -log(2), a = sol_a$roots), S2_D2 = list(r = sol_r6$roots, a = 6)), function(x) {
  d <- if (abs(x$r + log(2)) < 1e-12) dgm_r2 else build_cell(h = 2, r = x$r)
  ahr_design(ahr_population(d, 40, 11, entry_delay = list(var = "z_region", delay = x$a)), 0.55, 2, 1000)
})
for (k in names(dD)) {
  x <- if (k == "S2_D1") d1r else d2r; p <- dD[[k]]$prob
  stopifnot(abs(p[["p_itt_ub_lt1"]] - x$p_itt_ub_lt1) < 1e-6, abs(p[["p_region_itt_gt1"]] - x$p_region_itt_gt1) < 1e-6,
            abs(p[["p_trigger_and_Gstar_lt1"]] - x$p_trigger_Gstar_lt1) < 1e-6)
}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  cell = c("S2_D1", "S2_D2"), `r` = sprintf("−log %s", f3(exp(-c(-log(2), sol_r6$roots)))),
  `region delay a (months)` = f3(c(sol_a$roots, 6)),
  `P(ITT ub < 1.0)` = f3(vapply(dD, function(d) d$prob[["p_itt_ub_lt1"]], 0)),
  `P(region ITT > 1.0)` = f3(vapply(dD, function(d) d$prob[["p_region_itt_gt1"]], 0)),
  `P(trigger)` = f3(vapply(dD, function(d) d$prob[["p_trigger"]], 0)),
  `P(oracle joint)` = f3(vapply(dD, function(d) d$prob[["p_trigger_and_Gstar_lt1"]], 0)),
  `region margHR(40)` = f3(vapply(dD, function(d) d$sets$marghr[d$sets$set == "region"], 0)),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrrrr",
  caption = "The later-enrolling cells: roots reproduced with entry_delay (committed roots to 1e-6).")
t_an <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_an
```

A later-enrolling region is followed for less time, which keeps its 40-month window in the phase where
the treated $H^*$ patients are failing: a delay of `r f2(sol_a$roots)` months at $r = -\log 2$, or of 6
months at $r = -\log `r f3(exp(-sol_r6$roots))`$, does what the shift to $-\log 4$ does at no delay.
The analytic computations of this section took `r round(t_an)` seconds.

# Finding a case study {#sec-find}

The report's case example is one trial of the S2 cell, chosen by a stated rule: the first replicate,
by index, that reaches the trigger, declares $\hat H$ and has region($\hat G$) < 1.0. Four calls find
and examine such a trial in any simulation. They are shown on S2 with the campaign's arguments and
call seed at `r nsims_demo` replicates (`nsims_demo`, set at the top of the file), on workers from
`parallel::detectCores()`; with the campaign's seed these replicates are the campaign's first
`r nsims_demo`. The same run is summarised beside the campaign in @sec-demo.

**1. Simulate with the full record.** `mrct_region_sims(record = "full")` keeps, for every trial, the
Cox fits of the patient sets (the `"estimators"` attribute) that the selection reads.

```{r find-sims}
#| code-fold: show
seed_S2 <- cells$seed[cells$cell == "S2"]
confounders <- analysis_covariates(dgm_S2, "observed")
workers_demo <- max(1L, min(parallel::detectCores(), nsims_demo))
t_demo <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
demo <- mrct_region_sims(
  dgm_S2, n_sims = nsims_demo, n_sample = 1000, region_var = "z_region",
  sg_focus = "hrMaxSG", maxk = 2,
  hr.threshold = 0.90, hr.consistency = 0.80, pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,
  confounders.name = confounders, conf_force = character(0),
  fs_args = list(conf.cont_jcuts = list(z_cd40 = 10, z_wtkg = 10, z_preanti = 10),
                 effect_neighborhood = 0.20, use_grf = FALSE, use_lasso = FALSE),
  sim_args = list(rand_ratio = 1, draw_treatment = TRUE, max_entry = 11, cens_adjust = 50),
  analysis_time = 40, cens_adjust = 50,
  parallel_args = list(plan = "multisession", workers = workers_demo, show_message = FALSE),
  details = FALSE, verbose_n_sims = 0, seed = seed_S2, record = "full")
t_demo <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_demo
future::plan(future::sequential)
c(replicates = nsims_demo, workers = workers_demo, seconds = round(t_demo, 1))
```

**2. Select the trial.** `mrct_select_case()` flags every trial for the trigger, a declaration and
region($\hat G$) < 1.0, and returns the first meeting all three.

```{r find-select}
#| code-fold: show
case <- mrct_select_case(demo)
case
```

```{r find-select-check}
# the selection returns replicate 5, the report's case example
stopifnot(nrow(case) == 1, case$sim == 5)
est <- as.data.frame(attr(demo, "estimators")); demo <- as.data.frame(demo)[order(demo$sim), ]
stopifnot(nrow(demo) == nsims_demo, identical(demo$sim, seq_len(nsims_demo)))
# the campaign's first replicates, as the shipped record has them
trials5 <- rd("s2_example_trials.csv")
k5 <- intersect(trials5$sim, demo$sim)
stopifnot(near(demo$hr_itt[match(k5, demo$sim)], trials5$hr_itt[match(k5, trials5$sim)], 1e-10),
          near(demo$hr_test[match(k5, demo$sim)], trials5$hr_region[match(k5, trials5$sim)], 1e-10),
          identical(demo$sg_found[match(k5, demo$sim)], trials5$sg_found[match(k5, trials5$sim)]))
```

**3. Redraw and examine it.** `mrct_case_study()` redraws trial `k` exactly as the simulation drew it,
runs the identifier on its non-region patients with the simulation's arguments (the arguments
`mrct_region_sims()` takes directly go into `fs_args` here) followed by multiplier resampling, and
analyses the four sets.

```{r find-case}
#| code-fold: show
t_mr <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
cs <- mrct_case_study(
  dgm_S2, seed = seed_S2, k = case$sim, n = 1000, region_var = "z_region",
  fs_args = list(sg_focus = "hrMaxSG", maxk = 2,
                 hr.threshold = 0.90, hr.consistency = 0.80, pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,
                 confounders.name = confounders, conf_force = character(0),
                 conf.cont_jcuts = list(z_cd40 = 10, z_wtkg = 10, z_preanti = 10),
                 effect_neighborhood = 0.20, use_grf = FALSE, use_lasso = FALSE),
  sim_args = list(rand_ratio = 1, draw_treatment = TRUE, max_entry = 11, cens_adjust = 50),
  analysis_time = 40, cens_adjust = 50,
  mr_inference = TRUE,
  mr_inference_args = list(ci_method = "field", include_complement = TRUE, field_complement = TRUE,
                           draws = 2000, multiplier = "poisson", return_reselection = TRUE))
t_mr <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_mr
```

**4. Print and plot.** The four sets and the multiplier-resampling bounds for $\hat H$ and its
non-region complement; the forest plot of the four sets (`plot(cs)` also draws the Kaplan–Meier
panels, shown in @sec-rep5).

```{r find-print}
#| code-fold: show
print(cs)
```

```{r fig-case-forest}
#| code-fold: show
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.2
#| fig-cap: "Replicate 5 of S2: hazard ratio, experimental vs control, with 95% CI (log scale)."
plot(cs, which = "forest")
```

The selection returns replicate `r case$sim`, the report's case example; the rest of the article
examines that trial in detail.

# Replicate 5 of S2 {#sec-rep5}

Replicate $k$ of a cell was drawn under L'Ecuyer-CMRG by `simulate_from_dgm()` with seed equal to the
call seed plus $k$; `mrct_case_study()` redraws it that way and restores R's default generator.
Replicate 5 of S2 is the first triggered trial of the campaign's S2 cell meeting the rule of
@sec-find; its four hazard ratios and its $\hat H$ are shipped as the reproduction target.

```{r draw}
trial <- cs$trial
stopifnot(RNGkind()[1] == "Mersenne-Twister", cs$call_args$sim_args$seed == seed_S2 + 5)
c(seed = seed_S2 + 5, patients = nrow(trial), experimental = sum(trial$treat_sim == 1),
  events = sum(trial$event_sim), region = sum(trial$z_region == 1), non_region = sum(trial$z_region == 0))
```

## The identifier on the non-region patients, with post-selection inference {#sec-rep5-mr}

`forestsearch()` runs on the non-region patients, with the region's patients passed as the test set
to which the declared rule is applied, with the campaign's arguments: candidate cuts on the observed
covariates with deciles for CD4, weight and prior ART, at most two factors, hazard-ratio threshold 0.90
for screening and 0.80 for consistency at probability 0.90, the largest consistent subgroup within an
effect neighbourhood of 0.20 of the largest effect. Multiplier resampling (MR, `mr_inference = TRUE`)
follows in the same call: 2,000 Poisson multiplier draws, the complement de-biased and given its own
field (`include_complement`, `field_complement`), the field method at its default Monte Carlo sizes, the
re-selections returned, seed equal to the replicate's (`mrct_case_study()`'s default, `seed + k`). It
runs under R's default generator. The call of @sec-find made both steps; its arguments:

```{r identifier-mr}
fs <- cs$fs; mr <- cs$mr; Hhat_def <- cs$Hhat
# the identifier's arguments, as mrct_case_study() passed them to forestsearch()
a <- cs$call_args$fs_args
str(a[c("sg_focus", "maxk", "hr.threshold", "hr.consistency", "pconsistency.threshold",
        "effect_neighborhood", "conf_force", "conf.cont_jcuts", "use_grf", "use_lasso")])
str(a$mr_inference_args)
stopifnot(identical(a$confounders.name, confounders), a$mr_inference_args$seed == seed_S2 + 5,
          mr$ci_method == "field", mr$settings$draws == 2000, mr$field$n_out_used == mr$field$R_out)
c(seconds = round(t_mr, 1), candidate_family = mr$n_family, n_Hhat = mr$n_selected,
  n_Hhat_complement = mr$complement$n)
Hhat_def
```

$\hat H$ is `` `r Hhat_def` `` (`!{…}` is the complement): CD4 $\le$
`r sub(".*z_cd40 <= ([0-9.]+).*", "\\1", Hhat_def)` and prior ART over
`r sub(".*z_preanti <= ([0-9.]+).*", "\\1", Hhat_def)` days, against $H^*$ = CD4 $\le$ 230. The
case-study call took `r round(t_mr)` seconds on one thread.

**The Pareto frontier**: the admitted candidates that no other candidate beats on both hazard ratio
and size, with half-sample (split) 95% intervals from `compute_frontier_cis()` (1,000 random halvings
per member) and the effect neighbourhood 0.20 shaded; $\hat H$ is the selected member.

```{r frontier}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
ci_front <- compute_frontier_cis(fs, n_splits = 1000L, seed = seed_S2 + 5)
pf <- fs$grp.consistency$out_sg$pareto_frontier
stopifnot(nrow(ci_front) == nrow(pf), sum(pf$N == mr$n_selected & abs(pf$hr - mr$naive$est) < 1e-6) == 1)
print(plot_pareto_frontier(fs, ci_table = ci_front, show_band = TRUE, effect_neighborhood = 0.20))
```

**The inference table**, by `mr_estimates_table()` from the `forestsearch()` result alone. Two sets
are bounded, both among the non-region patients: $\hat H$ (row *Qstnbl*) and $\hat H^c$, its
non-region complement (row *Recmnd*). $\hat H^c$ is not $\hat G$; the region's outcomes play no part.

```{r mr-table}
mr_tab <- mr_estimates_table(fs, est.scale = "hr", digits = 3)
mv <- attr(mr_tab, "mr_values")
cc <- mr$complement; fl <- mr$field
stopifnot(near(mv$naive_est, c(mr$naive$est, cc$naive$est), 1e-12),
          near(mv$field_bound, c(fl$lower_1s, fl$complement$upper_1s), 1e-12),
          near(mv$bonferroni_bound, c(fl$joint$bonf_lower_H, fl$joint$bonf_upper_Hc), 1e-12))
mr_tab
```

```{r mr-repro}
# against the MR campaign's record of this replicate (same call, same seed)
mf <- rd("mr_field_S2_rep5.csv")
stopifnot(nrow(mf) == 1, mf$sim == 5, identical(mf$sg_found, Hhat_def),
          near(c(mv$naive_est[1], mv$debiased_est[1], mv$ij_lower[1], mv$ij_upper[1], mv$field_bound[1],
                 mv$naive_est[2], mv$debiased_est[2], mv$field_bound[2], mv$bonferroni_bound),
               c(mf$naive_H, mf$debiased_H, mf$ij_lower_H, mf$ij_upper_H, mf$field_lower_1s_H,
                 mf$naive_Hc, mf$debiased_Hc, mf$field_upper_1s_Hc, mf$bonf_lower_H, mf$bonf_upper_Hc), 1e-8),
          abs(mr$reselection$p_hat[[mr$selected_index]] - mf$p_hat_H) < 1e-12)
stopifnot(fl$lower_1s < 1, fl$complement$upper_1s < 1, mr$naive$est > mr$debiased$est)
c(p_hat_Hhat = mr$reselection$p_hat[[mr$selected_index]], selection_rate = mr$selection_rate)
```

The MR values equal the campaign's record of this replicate. Read by location: the naive hazard ratio
of $\hat H$ is `r f3(mr$naive$est)` and its de-biased value `r f3(mr$debiased$est)`, but the field
lower bound is `r f3(fl$lower_1s)`,
`r if (fl$lower_1s < 0.90) "below 0.90" else "above 0.90 but below 1.0"`:
once the selection is accounted for, the data do not rule out a modest benefit in $\hat H$. The field
upper bound for $\hat H^c$ is `r f3(fl$complement$upper_1s)`,
below 1.0: the non-region patients outside
$\hat H$ benefit. $\hat H$ is re-selected on a share
`r f3(mr$reselection$p_hat[[mr$selected_index]])` of the draws.

## The four sets

Each set is analysed by the unweighted two-sample Cox fit of treatment, with the Wald 95% interval.
$\hat H$ is read for every patient from the identifier's selected rule (`get_dfpred()`), checked against
its classification of the analysis and test sets. @fig-case-forest is their forest plot.

```{r four-sets}
in_Hhat <- cs$in_Hhat
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(trial$id),
          identical(in_Hhat, trial$id %in% c(fs$df.est$id[fs$df.est$treat.recommend == 0],
                                             fs$df.test$id[fs$df.test$treat.recommend == 0])))
reg <- trial$z_region == 1; Hstar <- trial$flag_harm == 1
set_label <- c(itt_all = "All patients, ITT", itt_region = "Region, ITT",
               region_Gstar = "Region minus H* (G*)", region_Ghat = "Region minus Ĥ (Ĝ)")
four <- cs$sets
stopifnot(identical(four$set, c("itt_all", "itt_region", "region_Gstar", "region_Ghat")))
knitr::kable(data.frame(Set = set_label[four$set], n = four$n,
                        `experimental n / events` = sprintf("%d / %d", four$n_exp, four$events_exp),
                        `control n / events` = sprintf("%d / %d", four$n_ctl, four$events_ctl),
                        HR = f3(four$hr), `95% CI` = sprintf("%s, %s", f3(four$lo), f3(four$hi)),
                        check.names = FALSE),
             row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrr", caption = "Replicate 5 of S2: the four sets.")
```

```{r km}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-cap: "Replicate 5 of S2: Kaplan–Meier by arm in the four sets (experimental blue, control black; months)."
plot(cs, which = "km")
```

The trial is positive (ITT upper limit `r f3(four$hi[1])` < 1.0) and its region is above 1.0
(`r f3(four$hr[2])`, `r four$events_exp[2] + four$events_ctl[2]` events): the trigger.

## $\hat H$ against $H^*$, in the region and outside

```{r hhat-vs-hstar}
cf_non <- cs$confusion$nonregion; cf_reg <- cs$confusion$region
sens <- function(x) x[["TP"]] / (x[["TP"]] + x[["FN"]]); spec <- function(x) x[["TN"]] / (x[["TN"]] + x[["FP"]])
knitr::kable(data.frame(population = c("non-region (where the identifier ran)", "region (where Ĥ is applied)"),
                        n = c(sum(!reg), sum(reg)),
                        TP = c(cf_non[["TP"]], cf_reg[["TP"]]), FP = c(cf_non[["FP"]], cf_reg[["FP"]]),
                        FN = c(cf_non[["FN"]], cf_reg[["FN"]]), TN = c(cf_non[["TN"]], cf_reg[["TN"]]),
                        Sens = f3(c(sens(cf_non), sens(cf_reg))), Spec = f3(c(spec(cf_non), spec(cf_reg)))),
             row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrrrr",
             caption = "Ĥ against H* = {CD4 ≤ 230}. TP: in Ĥ and in H*; FP: in Ĥ, not in H*; FN: in H*, not in Ĥ.")
hr4 <- setNames(four$hr, four$set)
stopifnot(hr4[["region_Gstar"]] < hr4[["region_Ghat"]], hr4[["region_Ghat"]] < 1, hr4[["itt_region"]] > 1)
```

$\hat H$ has the right variable and nearly the right cut, narrowed by prior therapy: it finds about
half of the harmed patients (Sens `r f3(sens(cf_non))` outside the region) and almost no one else
(Spec `r f3(spec(cf_non))`). Applied in the region it removes `r sum(in_Hhat & reg)` patients,
`r cf_reg[["TP"]]` of them in $H^*$, and region($\hat G$) is `r f3(four$hr[four$set == "region_Ghat"])`,
between the whole region and the oracle region($G^*$) = `r f3(four$hr[four$set == "region_Gstar"])`, as a
partial removal of $H^*$ should. Every interval is wide: the regional sets have few events, so the move
of the regional estimate from above 1 to below 1 is an explanation consistent with a trial-wide harmed
subgroup, not confirmation of it.

## Reproduction check against the committed record

The four hazard ratios must equal the shipped record to three decimals with the same counts, $\hat H$
the committed definition, and the $2 \times 2$ tables the committed ones; the article stops otherwise.

```{r reproduction}
rec <- rd("s2_example_four_sets.csv", colClasses = c(hr_3dp = "character", ci_3dp = "character"))
rec <- rec[match(four$set, rec$set), ]
trials5 <- rd("s2_example_trials.csv")
defs <- readLines(file.path(dd, "s2_example_definitions.md"))
rec2x2 <- function(lab) {
  l <- defs[grepl(paste0("^- ", lab, "( \\(|:)"), defs)]; stopifnot(length(l) == 1)
  vapply(c(TP = "TP", FP = "FP", FN = "FN", TN = "TN"),
         function(k) as.integer(sub(sprintf(".*%s ([0-9]+).*", k), "\\1", l)), 0L)
}
stopifnot(identical(rec$set, four$set), all(rec$sim == 5),
          identical(f3(four$hr), rec$hr_3dp),
          all(four$n == rec$n, four$events_exp == rec$events_exp, four$events_ctl == rec$events_ctl),
          identical(Hhat_def, trials5$sg_found[trials5$sim == 5]),
          identical(cf_reg, rec2x2("Region")), identical(cf_non, rec2x2("Non-region")))
knitr::kable(data.frame(set = set_label[four$set], reproduced = f3(four$hr), committed = rec$hr_3dp,
                        abs_difference = signif(abs(four$hr - rec$hr), 2)), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Reproduced against the committed hazard ratios.")
```

**Passed** under forestsearch `r as.character(packageVersion("forestsearch"))`: the four hazard ratios
(largest absolute difference `r format(max(abs(four$hr - rec$hr)), digits = 2)`), the counts, $\hat H$ and
both $2 \times 2$ tables equal the record.

## The four sets beside their limits

The analytic layer's limit of each set's Cox estimate, with the set's AHR and CDE; $\hat G$ is
replicate 5's rule applied to every super-population row of the region. $z$ is the estimate's distance
from its limit in units of the robust SE that the limit implies at the set's size.

```{r rep5-limits}
Hhat_super <- get_dfpred(dgm_S2$df_super, sg.harm = fs$sg.harm, version = 2)$treat.recommend == 0
lim_sets <- list(itt_all = "all", itt_region = "region", region_Gstar = "region_Gstar",
                 region_Ghat = pop_S2$region & !Hhat_super)
lims <- lapply(lim_sets, function(s) ahr_limit(pop_S2, s, b = 0.55, h = 2, variance = TRUE))
z <- (log(four$hr) - vapply(lims[four$set], `[[`, 0, "beta")) /
  sqrt(vapply(lims[four$set], `[[`, 0, "var_robust") / four$n)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Set = set_label[four$set], `replicate 5 HR` = f3(four$hr),
  `margHR(40)` = f3(vapply(lims[four$set], `[[`, 0, "hr")), `margHR(∞)` = f3(vapply(lims[four$set], `[[`, 0, "marghr_inf")),
  AHR = f3(vapply(lims[four$set], `[[`, 0, "ahr")), CDE = f3(vapply(lims[four$set], `[[`, 0, "cde")),
  z = f2(z), check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrrr",
  caption = "Replicate 5 of S2: the estimates beside the analytic limits of their sets.")
stopifnot(lims$itt_region$hr < 1, z[four$set == "itt_region"] > 0)
```

The region's limit, margHR(40) = `r f3(lims$itt_region$hr)`, is below 1; replicate 5's regional
estimate sits `r f2(z[four$set == "itt_region"])` robust SDs above it. A regional prognostic effect, a
harmed subgroup and a finite window move the region's limit toward 1, and sampling did the rest.

# Simulation results {#sec-sims}

The campaign ran 10,000 replicates per cell at $n = 1{,}000$ with `mrct_region_sims()`. Its records are
summarised here from the shipped core tables; @sec-demo summarises the small run of @sec-find beside them.

## The core operating characteristics at $n = 1{,}000$

```{r core-n1000}
core <- rd("core_n1000.csv")
cn <- rbind(rd("core_full_numeric.csv"), rd("core_S1_numeric.csv")[, names(rd("core_full_numeric.csv"))])
cn <- cn[cn$setting %in% paste0(cells6$cell, "_rmlog4"), ]
ord6 <- c("N0", "N1", "S1", "S2", "S3", "S4")
wide <- reshape(core[, c("row", "label", "column", "value")], idvar = c("row", "label"), timevar = "column",
                direction = "wide")
names(wide) <- sub("^value\\.", "", names(wide))
wide <- wide[order(as.integer(sub("r", "", wide$row))), c("label", ord6)]
# recount: each cell of the table from the counts of the numeric core tables
lead <- function(x) sub("^([0-9.,]+).*$", "\\1", x)          # the leading number, as printed
p1 <- function(k, n) sprintf("%.1f", 100 * k / n)
for (k in ord6) {
  x <- cn[cn$setting == paste0(k, "_rmlog4"), ]; v <- core[core$column == k, ]; g <- function(r) v$value[v$row == r]
  of <- as.numeric(gsub(",", "", sub("^.*SE [0-9.]+; ([0-9,]+) of [0-9,]+\\)$", "\\1", g("r1"))))
  stopifnot(nrow(x) == 1, x$replicates == 10000,
            lead(g("r1")) == p1(of, x$replicates),
            lead(g("r2")) == big(x$n_trigger),
            lead(g("r3")) == p1(x$n_declared, x$n_trigger),
            lead(g("r6")) == p1(x$n_declared_Ghat_lt1, x$n_trigger),
            lead(g("r7")) == p1(x$n_Gstar_lt1, x$n_trigger),
            lead(g("r8")) == p1(x$n_declared_Ghat_ge1, x$n_trigger),
            x$n_declared_Ghat_lt1 + x$n_declared_Ghat_ge1 == x$n_declared)
}
# the reading's verbal claims
xs <- cn[match(paste0(ord6, "_rmlog4"), cn$setting), ]; rownames(xs) <- ord6
stopifnot(!is.unsorted(xs$n_trigger), all(xs[c("S2", "S3", "S4"), "pct_declared"] > 99.9),
          all(xs[c("S2", "S3", "S4"), "sens_nonregion"] > 55 & xs[c("S2", "S3", "S4"), "sens_nonregion"] < 65),
          all(xs[c("S2", "S3", "S4"), "spec_nonregion"] > 95))
knitr::kable(wide, row.names = FALSE, align = c("l", rep("r", 6)),
             caption = "Core operating characteristics, n = 1,000, 10,000 replicates per cell. Rows 3–8 are % of the triggered trials (Sens / Spec averaged over the declared triggered trials), with binomial SE.")
```

Every count-derived entry equals its recount from the numeric records. Reading: the trigger becomes more
frequent as the harm in $H^*$ grows (from `r big(cn$n_trigger[cn$setting == "N0_rmlog4"])` triggered trials
in N0 to `r big(cn$n_trigger[cn$setting == "S4_rmlog4"])` in S4). Where there is something to find (S2–S4)
a subgroup is declared in essentially every triggered trial, it overlaps $H^*$ with sensitivity about 0.6
and specificity above 0.95, and the joint holds in
`r pc(cn$n_declared_Ghat_lt1[cn$setting == "S2_rmlog4"] / cn$n_trigger[cn$setting == "S2_rmlog4"])`% to
`r pc(cn$n_declared_Ghat_lt1[cn$setting == "S4_rmlog4"] / cn$n_trigger[cn$setting == "S4_rmlog4"])`% of
triggered trials, against an oracle ceiling of
`r pc(cn$n_Gstar_lt1[cn$setting == "S2_rmlog4"] / cn$n_trigger[cn$setting == "S2_rmlog4"])`% to
`r pc(cn$n_Gstar_lt1[cn$setting == "S4_rmlog4"] / cn$n_trigger[cn$setting == "S4_rmlog4"])`%. Where there
is nothing harmful to find (N0) a subgroup is still declared in
`r pc(cn$n_declared[cn$setting == "N0_rmlog4"] / cn$n_trigger[cn$setting == "N0_rmlog4"])`% of triggered
trials and the joint holds in
`r pc(cn$n_declared_Ghat_lt1[cn$setting == "N0_rmlog4"] / cn$n_trigger[cn$setting == "N0_rmlog4"])`%: the
strategy "explains" some triggers when there is nothing to explain, which is why it is signal
generation.

## The later-enrolling cells

```{r core-entry}
ce <- rd("entry_cells_core.csv"); cen <- rd("entry_cells_core_numeric.csv")
gv <- function(q, k) cen[[k]][cen$quantity == q]
for (k in c("S2", "S2_D1", "S2_D2")) {
  stopifnot(abs(gv("trigger_pct", k) - 100 * gv("trigger_n", k) / gv("n_trials", k)) < 1e-9,
            abs(gv("p_trigger", k) - gv("trigger_n", k) / gv("n_trials", k)) < 1e-12,
            lead(ce[[k]][ce$row == "r2"]) == sprintf("%.1f", gv("trigger_pct", k)),
            grepl(sprintf("(%s)", big(gv("trigger_n", k))), ce[[k]][ce$row == "r2"], fixed = TRUE),
            lead(ce[[k]][ce$row == "r8"]) == sprintf("%.1f", gv("joint", k)),
            lead(ce[[k]][ce$row == "r9"]) == sprintf("%.1f", gv("oracle", k)))
}
# the S2 column is the n = 1,000 campaign's S2 cell
x2 <- cn[cn$setting == "S2_rmlog4", ]
stopifnot(gv("trigger_n", "S2") == x2$n_trigger,
          abs(gv("joint", "S2") - 100 * x2$n_declared_Ghat_lt1 / x2$n_trigger) < 1e-9)
knitr::kable(ce[, c("label", "denominator", "S2", "S2_D1", "S2_D2")], row.names = FALSE,
             align = "llrrr", caption = "S2 at no delay and the two later-enrolling cells, 10,000 replicates each.")
```

The later-enrolling cells behave as S2: the same trigger rate by construction, the same
identification and nearly the same joint
(`r f2(gv("joint", "S2_D1"))`% and `r f2(gv("joint", "S2_D2"))`% against `r f2(gv("joint", "S2"))`%).
What makes the region look inconsistent does not need to be a prognostic shift: a shorter regional
follow-up does the same.

## Predicted against observed

The analytic layer's trigger probability and oracle joint (computed in @sec-analytic) against the
campaign's frequencies over 10,000 trials, with $z$ the difference in binomial SEs.

```{r pred-obs}
po <- rbind(
  data.frame(cell = d1000$cell, pred_trigger = d1000$p_A_B, pred_oracle = d1000$p_A_B_Cstar,
             obs_trigger = cn$n_trigger[match(paste0(d1000$cell, "_rmlog4"), cn$setting)] / 10000,
             obs_oracle = cn$n_Gstar_lt1[match(paste0(d1000$cell, "_rmlog4"), cn$setting)] / 10000),
  data.frame(cell = names(dD), pred_trigger = vapply(dD, function(d) d$prob[["p_trigger"]], 0),
             pred_oracle = vapply(dD, function(d) d$prob[["p_trigger_and_Gstar_lt1"]], 0),
             obs_trigger = vapply(names(dD), gv, 0, q = "p_trigger"),
             obs_oracle = vapply(names(dD), gv, 0, q = "p_trigger_Gstar_lt1")))
zb <- function(o, p) (o - p) / sqrt(p * (1 - p) / 10000)
po$z_trigger <- zb(po$obs_trigger, po$pred_trigger); po$z_oracle <- zb(po$obs_oracle, po$pred_oracle)
knitr::kable(data.frame(cell = po$cell, `P(trigger): predicted` = f4(po$pred_trigger), observed = f4(po$obs_trigger),
                        z = f2(po$z_trigger), `oracle joint: predicted` = f4(po$pred_oracle),
                        `observed ` = f4(po$obs_oracle), `z ` = f2(po$z_oracle), check.names = FALSE),
             row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrrr",
             caption = "Analytic predictions against the campaign (10,000 trials per cell).")
```

The normal approximation predicts the trigger and the oracle joint before any simulation; the largest
$|z|$ over the eight cells is `r f2(max(abs(c(po$z_trigger, po$z_oracle))))`.

## Post-selection inference on $\hat H$ in the triggered trials

The MR field call of @sec-rep5-mr was run on every triggered trial of the eight cells. Three shares
are read by location, against clinically meaningful hazard ratios: the share of declared triggered
trials whose $\hat H$ lower bound is above 0.90 and above 1.0, and the share whose $\hat H^c$ upper
bound is below 1.0.

```{r mr-field}
mfc <- rd("mr_field_core.csv")
knitr::kable(mfc[, -1], row.names = FALSE, align = c("l", rep("r", 8)),
             caption = "MR field inference on the triggered trials (rows 1–3: % of declared triggered trials).")
mv_ <- function(row, k) mfc[[k]][mfc$row == row]
stopifnot(max(vapply(c("N0", "N1", "S1"), mv_, 0, row = "lb_090")) < 1)
```

Reading: where there is nothing harmful to find (N0, N1, S1) the lower bound for $\hat H$ almost never
excludes a hazard ratio of 0.90 (`r f2(max(vapply(c("N0", "N1", "S1"), mv_, 0, row = "lb_090")))`% at
most): the bound does not mistake a selected subgroup for a harmed one. With harm $h = 2$ (S2) it
excludes 0.90 in `r f2(mv_("lb_090", "S2"))`% of declared triggered trials and 1.0 in
`r f2(mv_("lb_100", "S2"))`%; with $h = 4$ in `r f2(mv_("lb_090", "S4"))`% and `r f2(mv_("lb_100", "S4"))`%.
The upper bound for $\hat H^c$ is below 1.0 in every cell's declared triggered trials
(`r f2(min(vapply(setdiff(names(mfc), c("row", "label")), mv_, 0, row = "ubc_100")))`% at least): the
patients outside $\hat H$ benefit. The spread between the de-biased estimate and the bound is the price
of the selection.

## The campaign code and its wall-clock {#sec-campaign-code}

The committed campaign, one `mrct_region_sims()` call per cell, with every argument (shown, not run):

```{r campaign-code, eval = FALSE}
campaign_cell <- function(dgm, seed, n_sims = 10000L, workers = 64L, entry_delay = NULL) {
  mrct_region_sims(
    dgm, n_sims = n_sims, n_sample = 1000, region_var = "z_region",
    sg_focus = "hrMaxSG", maxk = 2,
    hr.threshold = 0.90, hr.consistency = 0.80, pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,
    confounders.name = analysis_covariates(dgm, "observed"), conf_force = character(0),
    fs_args = list(conf.cont_jcuts = list(z_cd40 = 10, z_wtkg = 10, z_preanti = 10),
                   effect_neighborhood = 0.20, use_grf = FALSE, use_lasso = FALSE),
    sim_args = list(rand_ratio = 1, draw_treatment = TRUE, max_entry = 11, cens_adjust = 50,
                    entry_delay = entry_delay),
    analysis_time = 40, cens_adjust = 50,
    parallel_args = list(plan = "multisession", workers = workers, show_message = FALSE),
    details = FALSE, seed = seed, record = "full")
}
# the six cells at r = -log 4
for (k in c("N0", "N1", "S1", "S2", "S3", "S4"))
  res[[k]] <- campaign_cell(build_cell(h = cells$h[cells$cell == k]), seed = cells$seed[cells$cell == k])
# the later-enrolling cells: the region enters a months later
res$S2_D1 <- campaign_cell(build_cell(h = 2, r = -log(2)), seed = cells$seed[cells$cell == "S2_D1"],
                           entry_delay = list(var = "z_region", delay = sol_a$roots))
res$S2_D2 <- campaign_cell(build_cell(h = 2, r = sol_r6$roots), seed = cells$seed[cells$cell == "S2_D2"],
                           entry_delay = list(var = "z_region", delay = 6))
```

The committed runs predate `record = "full"` and `entry_delay`: their per-replicate records were
rebuilt by redrawing each trial from its seed, which `record = "full"` now returns directly from the
same trials, and the later-enrolling cells stored a fixed entry time per super-population row
(`entry_var`), where `entry_delay` redraws the entry each trial with the same law. The timing records:

```{r wall-clock}
tm <- rbind(data.frame(cell = sub("_rmlog4$", "", tf$setting), workers = tf$workers, wall_sec = tf$wall_sec),
            data.frame(cell = "S1", workers = ts1$workers[ts1$setting == "S1_rmlog4"], wall_sec = ts1$wall_sec[ts1$setting == "S1_rmlog4"]),
            data.frame(cell = te$setting, workers = te$workers, wall_sec = te$wall_sec))
tm <- tm[match(cells$cell, tm$cell), ]
mft <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cells$cell, function(k) {
  x <- rd(sprintf("timing_mr_field_%s.csv", k))
  data.frame(cell = k, mr_trials = sum(x$trials_run_this_session), mr_workers = x$workers[1], mr_wall_sec = sum(x$wall_sec))
}))
stopifnot(identical(mft$cell, tm$cell))
knitr::kable(data.frame(cell = tm$cell, `simulation: workers` = tm$workers, `simulation: wall-clock (min)` = f2(tm$wall_sec / 60),
                        `MR field: triggered trials` = big(mft$mr_trials), `MR field: workers` = mft$mr_workers,
                        `MR field: wall-clock (min)` = f2(mft$mr_wall_sec / 60), check.names = FALSE),
             row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrr", caption = "Wall-clock of the committed runs, from their timing records.")
```

The five cells N0–S4 ran side by side (the longest took `r f2(max(tf$wall_sec) / 3600)` hours on
`r tf$workers[1]` workers each), S1 took `r round(ts1$wall_sec[ts1$setting == "S1_rmlog4"] / 60)` minutes and the
two later-enrolling cells `r round(te$wall_sec[1] / 60)` and `r round(te$wall_sec[2] / 60)` minutes, one after
the other. The MR field campaign ran the eight cells one after another on the
`r big(sum(mft$mr_trials))` triggered trials in `r f2(sum(mft$mr_wall_sec) / 3600)` hours.

## The demonstration run {#sec-demo}

The run of @sec-find (`r nsims_demo` replicates of S2 with the campaign's arguments and call seed, on
`r workers_demo` workers, `r round(t_demo)` seconds), summarised into the core rows by the definitions of
the core table. With the campaign's seed, its replicates are the campaign's first `r nsims_demo`; @sec-find
checks its first replicates against the shipped record.

```{r demo-summary}
g_est <- function(k) { y <- est[est$estimator == k, ]; y[match(demo$sim, y$sim), ] }
itt <- g_est("itt_all"); rgn <- g_est("itt_region"); gh <- g_est("region_Ghat"); gs <- g_est("region_Gstar")
lt1 <- function(v) !is.na(v) & v < 1; gt1 <- function(v) !is.na(v) & v > 1
A <- lt1(itt$hi); K <- A & gt1(rgn$hr); dec <- demo$any_found == 1; DK <- dec & K
ss <- function(tp, fn) tp / (tp + fn)
sens_non <- with(demo, ss(TP_nonregion, FN_nonregion)); spec_non <- with(demo, ss(TN_nonregion, FP_nonregion))
sens_reg <- with(demo, ss(TP_region, FN_region)); spec_reg <- with(demo, ss(TN_region, FP_region))
pk <- function(w, d = K) if (sum(d)) pc(sum(w & d) / sum(d)) else "–"
av <- function(v) if (sum(DK)) pc(mean(v[DK], na.rm = TRUE)) else "–"
demo_rows <- data.frame(
  row = c("trial power (ITT ub < 1.0)", "trials reaching the trigger (count)", "subgroup declared",
          "Sens / Spec of Ĥ vs H*, non-region", "Sens / Spec of Ĥ vs H*, region",
          "declared, region(Ĝ) < 1.0", "region(G*) < 1.0", "declared, region(Ĝ) ≥ 1.0"),
  demonstration = c(pc(mean(A)), sprintf("%d of %d", sum(K), nsims_demo), pk(dec),
                    paste(av(sens_non), "/", av(spec_non)), paste(av(sens_reg), "/", av(spec_reg)),
                    pk(dec & lt1(gh$hr)), pk(lt1(gs$hr)), pk(dec & !lt1(gh$hr))),
  campaign = wide$S2)
knitr::kable(demo_rows, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrr",
             col.names = c("", sprintf("demonstration (%d replicates)", nsims_demo), "campaign (10,000)"),
             caption = "The core rows of S2: the live demonstration beside the committed campaign (rows 3–8 in % of triggered trials).")
```

At `r nsims_demo` replicates the demonstration has `r sum(K)` triggered trials, so its rows carry
large Monte Carlo error; they are a check of the pipeline, not an estimate of its operating
characteristics. The whole article took
`r round((proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_article) / 60, 1)` minutes to run.

# Appendix: the analytic tools {#sec-appendix}

This appendix condenses the analytic chapter of the technical report (Chapter 6, "The analytic layer";
theory notes `AHR_mrct_dgm.qmd` and `AHR_complete.qmd` of the mrct-consistency repository), where the
derivations are.

**The DGM in closed form.** The Weibull AFT draws $\log T = \mu + \ell_z(x) + \tau\varepsilon$ with
$\varepsilon = \log \mathrm{Exp}(1)$, so
$$
\bar F(s \mid x, z) = \exp\{-\Lambda_0(s)\, e^{\theta_z(x)}\}, \qquad
\Lambda_0(s) = (s e^{-\mu})^{1/\tau}, \qquad \theta_z(x) = -\ell_z(x)/\tau ,
$$
a proportional-hazards model in $(x, z)$ with Weibull baseline. The prognostic part is
$\theta_0(x) = x^\top\beta + r\,\mathbf 1\{x \in R\}$, the treatment effect
$\psi(x) = \theta_1(x) - \theta_0(x) = \log b + \log(h/b)\,\mathbf 1\{\mathrm{CD4} \le 230\}$, and
`scale_dgm_hazard()` sets $\mu \leftarrow \mu_{\text{fit}} - \tau \log m$, multiplying every hazard by
$m$ and leaving every $\theta$ unchanged.

**The counting-process setting and the least-false limit.** On a patient set $\mathcal S$ with entry
$E \sim U(0, t_e)$ and analysis at calendar time $t_a$ (here 11 and 40 months), patient $i$ has window
$t_a - E_i$, at-risk process $Y_i(s)$ and counting process $N_i(s)$. The two-sample Cox estimate
$\hat\beta_{\mathcal S}$ is the root of the partial-likelihood score
$U_{n,\mathcal S}(\beta) = \sum_{i \in \mathcal S}\int_0^{t_a}\{Z_i - \bar Z_{\mathcal S}(s, \beta)\}\,dN_i(s)$,
$\bar Z_{\mathcal S} = S^{(1)}_{\mathcal S}/S^{(0)}_{\mathcal S}$. The model is misspecified (the set
mixes patients with different hazard ratios), and $\hat\beta_{\mathcal S}$ converges to the least-false
parameter $\beta^*_{\mathcal S}$, the root of the population score (Struthers and Kalbfleisch 1986;
Gerds and Schumacher 2001); margHR(40) $= e^{\beta^*_{\mathcal S}}$. Breslow's estimator converges to
$\Lambda_0^*$, with $\lambda_0^*/\lambda_0 = (f_1 + f_0)/(e^{\beta^*}A_1 + A_0)$ in operational time.

**The Struthers–Kalbfleisch root for a patient set.** In operational time $u = \Lambda_0(s)$ patient $i$
on arm $z$ is exponential with rate $e^{\theta_{z,i}}$; with
$A_z(u) = |\mathcal S|^{-1}\sum_{\mathcal S} e^{-u e^{\theta_{z,i}}}$, $f_z = -A_z'$ and the entry factor
$H_w(u) = H(t_a - \Lambda_0^{-1}(u))$, $H$ the entry distribution function, the limit is the unique root of
$$
\begin{aligned}
U_{\mathcal S}(\beta) &= \tfrac12 \int_0^{\Lambda_0(t_a)} H_w(u)\Bigl\{f_1(u) - r(u, \beta)\,[f_1(u) + f_0(u)]\Bigr\}\,du,\\
r(u, \beta) &= \frac{e^\beta A_1(u)}{e^\beta A_1(u) + A_0(u)} ,
\end{aligned}
$$
and margHR($\infty$) is the root with $H_w \equiv 1$ to $u = \infty$. $\partial U/\partial\beta < 0$, so
the root is unique. With $\delta(u) = \log\{A_1/A_0\}$ and the set's instantaneous hazard ratio
$\vartheta_{\mathcal S}(u) = (f_1/A_1)/(f_0/A_0)$ the score is
$\int\{\operatorname{expit}(\log\vartheta_{\mathcal S} + \delta) - \operatorname{expit}(\beta + \delta)\}\,dN$,
$dN = \tfrac12 H_w (f_1 + f_0)\,du$: the score of a time-varying-effect model whose profile is induced by
composition. `ahr_limit()` evaluates the arm functions as finite sums over the super-population rows of
the set, integrates by composite Gauss–Legendre quadrature on geometric panels in $u$ with breaks at the
entry kinks, and finds the root by `uniroot()`. The set's other truths are
$$
\mathrm{AHR}(\mathcal S) = \exp\Bigl\{\tfrac1{|\mathcal S|}\textstyle\sum_{\mathcal S}\psi\Bigr\} = b^{1 - p_{\mathcal S}} h^{p_{\mathcal S}},
\qquad
\mathrm{CDE}(\mathcal S) = \frac{\sum_{\mathcal S} e^{\theta_1}}{\sum_{\mathcal S} e^{\theta_0}} = (1 - \omega^0_{\mathcal S})\,b + \omega^0_{\mathcal S}\,h ,
$$
$p_{\mathcal S}$ the set's $H^*$ share and $\omega^0_{\mathcal S}$ the share of its baseline hazard carried by $H^*$.

**The clock identity and the frailty reading.** Under a uniform effect ($h = b$),
$A_1(u) = L_{\mathcal S}(bu)$ and $A_0(u) = L_{\mathcal S}(u)$ with $L_{\mathcal S}$ the Laplace transform
of $e^{\theta_0}$ over the set: the covariate-driven baseline acts as a frailty, and
$\vartheta_{\mathcal S}(s) = b\,\ell_{\mathcal S}(b\Lambda_0(s))/\ell_{\mathcal S}(\Lambda_0(s))$, with
$\ell_{\mathcal S}$ the survival-weighted mean of $e^{\theta_0}$ among the set's survivors, drifts from $b$
toward 1 as high-hazard patients leave. The regional shift adds $r$ to $\theta_0$ on every region row, so
for a set inside the region every arm function at $r$ is the function at $r = 0$ evaluated at $e^r u$:
**$r$ is a clock on the region**. margHR($\infty$), the AHR and the CDE do not see $r$; only the windowed
margHR(40) moves. With a harmed $H^*$ the region's profile starts at its CDE, above 1, while the treated
$H^*$ patients fail, crosses 1 once they are spent and settles near $b$; the slower clock keeps the
40-month window in the harm phase and moves the region's margHR(40) toward the null. A regional
prognostic effect, a harmed subgroup and a finite window are needed together.

**The first-order and events forms.** Setting every imbalance to zero gives
$$
\operatorname{expit}(\beta^*_{\mathcal S}) \approx (1 - \omega_{\mathcal S})\frac{b}{1+b} + \omega_{\mathcal S}\frac{h}{1+h},
$$
$\omega_{\mathcal S}$ the share of the set's expected events in the window carried by $H^*$, with a
closed form through the event probability
$\pi(\theta) = 1 - \tfrac{1}{t_e}\int_{t_a - t_e}^{t_a}\exp\{-c\,w^{1/\tau}\}\,dw$, $c = e^{\theta - \mu/\tau}$.
It fails for a harmed $H^*$, whose treated patients are used up early. Exactly, the score equation is
$D_1/(D_1 + D_0) = \langle\operatorname{expit}(\beta^* + \delta)\rangle_N$, $D_z$ the arms' event
probabilities and $\langle\cdot\rangle_N$ the events-weighted average over the window; expanded about
$\bar\delta = \langle\delta\rangle_N$,
$$
\beta^* \approx \log\frac{D_1}{D_0} - \bar\delta - \tfrac12(1 - 2\bar P)\,\mathrm{Var}_N(\delta),
\qquad \bar P = \frac{D_1}{D_1 + D_0}:
$$
the marginal hazard ratio is the ratio of the arms' event probabilities divided by the geometric-mean
ratio of the arms' numbers at risk at the event times.

**The design layer.** For a trial of $n$ patients, 1:1, with $n_{\mathcal S} \sim \mathrm{Bin}(n, \pi_{\mathcal S})$
in $\mathcal S$ and $i_1 = \int r(1 - r)\,dN$ the information per patient,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{Var}(\hat\beta_{\mathcal S}) &\approx \frac{1}{i_1}\,\mathrm E\Bigl[\frac{1}{n_{\mathcal S}}\Bigr] && \text{(model)},\\
&\approx \frac{\Sigma}{i_1^2}\,\mathrm E\Bigl[\frac{1}{n_{\mathcal S}}\Bigr] && \text{(robust)},\\
\mathrm E\Bigl[\frac{1}{n_{\mathcal S}}\Bigr] &\approx \frac{1}{n\pi_{\mathcal S}}\Bigl\{1 + \frac{1 - \pi_{\mathcal S}}{n\pi_{\mathcal S}}\Bigr\},
\end{aligned}
$$
$\Sigma$ the variance of the Lin–Wei influence. Under a common proportional-hazards model the
correlation of nested estimates is the square root of the information share,
$\rho = \mathrm{Corr}(\hat\beta_{\text{all}}, \hat\beta_R) = \sqrt{I_R/I_{\text{all}}}$; under
misspecification the layer uses the exact covariance of the two influences. With $\mu_{\mathcal S} = \beta^*_{\mathcal S}$,
$\sigma_{\mathcal S}$ the robust SD, $\tilde\sigma_{\text{all}}$ the model SE and $z = 1.96$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
P(\text{ITT ub} < 1) &= \Phi(z_A), & z_A &= \frac{-z\tilde\sigma_{\text{all}} - \mu_{\text{all}}}{\sigma_{\text{all}}};\\
P(\text{region ITT} > 1) &= \Phi(-z_B), & z_B &= \frac{-\mu_R}{\sigma_R};\\
P(\text{trigger}) &= \Phi_2(z_A, -z_B; -\rho_{\text{all},R}),
\end{aligned}
$$
and the oracle joint is the trivariate $\Phi_3(z_A, -z_B, z_C; \mathbf R)$ with
$z_C = -\mu_{G^*}/\sigma_{G^*}$, $\mathbf R$ the correlation matrix of
$(\hat\beta_{\text{all}}, -\hat\beta_R, \hat\beta_{G^*})$ (`ahr_design()`).

**Per-patient entry.** With `entry_delay`, patient $i$ enters at $a_i + E$, $E \sim U(0, t_e)$; each
patient carries their own entry factor $H_{w,i}(u)$, and the arm functions of the score become the
entry-weighted sums $A_{H}(u) = |\mathcal S|^{-1}\sum_{\mathcal S} H_{w,i}(u)\,e^{-u e^{\theta_{1,i}}}$ (and
likewise for the control arm and the event densities), with quadrature breaks at each entry group's
kinks. For a set inside a region delayed by $a$, the limit equals the undelayed limit at horizon
$t_a - a$: a later-enrolling region is a region analysed earlier. With no delay every $H_{w,i}$ is the
common $H_w$ and the layer is the one above.
